entries.title: Wildfire in southern Spain leaves at least 12 dead and 23 missing
entries.snippet: A local official said four of the victims may be British after a fire broke out near Los Gallardos, Almería.

entries.title: Meet the crypto billionaires building a world where money buys you a vote
entries.snippet: They think democracy has run its course - so they're setting up their own nations instead.

entries.title: East Asia braces for destructive typhoon as landslides kill 15 in Philippines
entries.snippet: Heading for Taiwan and south-eastern China, the 1,000 km-wide Bavi is forecast to be one of the strongest storms in decades.

entries.title: Forced to wait his turn, Marine Le Pen's deputy Bardella returns to the shadows
entries.snippet: Thirty-year-old Jordan Bardella had been groomed for success as France's next hard-right leader. He will now have to wait longer.

entries.title: Zulu king expresses regret after video captures tirade against his wife
entries.snippet: In the footage widely shared in South Africa, King Misuzulu threatens to physically assault his wife and accuses her of cheating.

entries.snippet: Immigration agents were looking for a different person when they shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a traffic stop, officials say.

entries.title: Man nearly sucked out of window mid-air on Ryanair plane, passengers say
entries.snippet: The man's wife held onto his legs for around five minutes to stop him from being sucked out, officials say.

entries.title: New dinosaur species with neck as long as cricket pitch discovered in Thailand
entries.snippet: The plant-eating dinosaur, named Uragasaurus kalasinensis, is thought to have lived about 150 million years ago.

entries.title: Meta pulls new AI image feature after days of backlash
entries.snippet: Meta's release this week of an AI feature that let people alter Instagram content drew swift blowback.

entries.title: Nolan Wells' family demands answers about US teen's death after boating trip

entries.title: How a fake presidential council ended up with a budget of almost $1m in Nigeria
entries.snippet: The government says it was set up with a forged letter of appointment but others say there is more to it.

entries.title: At Canada's biggest rodeo, the starting gun is fired in the fight over Alberta separation
entries.snippet: Canadian unity takes centre stage at the Calgary Stampede as fears of a Brexit-style upset looms over the October vote on Alberta's future.

entries.title: Twelve men and 12 women enter a Buddhist temple - will the monks help them find love?
entries.snippet: Dating can be hard in South Korea. A group of monks hope a 30-hour rural retreat can help.

entries.title: Boxy forms and odd lights: US declassifies more UFO files
entries.snippet: The US government published a fourth instalment of unresolved cases, promising to release more files on a rolling basis.

entries.title: Watch: What links a bomb in Monaco and a shooting in Ukraine?
entries.snippet: A Ukrainian intelligence agent who confessed to killing the woman suspected of trying to assassinate a multimillionaire in Monaco, has now claimed he did not pull the trigger.

entries.title: Graham Platner makes it official in Maine, submitting paperwork to leave Senate race
entries.snippet: In his withdrawal notice, Platner said "people are desperate for change" and that's why they made him the Democratic nominee. Now, Maine Democrats have to pick someone to replace him by July 27.

entries.title: Patriotic art gets the spotlight as NEA funding shifts. Cue 'The Ronald Reagan Overture'
entries.snippet: Patriotic art and music is taking center stage this year under the Trump Administration, as funds shift away from DEI. For some orgs, like the Reagan Presidential Library, this is their wheelhouse.

entries.title: Houston neighbors started seeing more ICE agents around. Then came a fatal shooting.
entries.snippet: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was a 52-year-old Mexican national who worked in construction for more than three decades. The father of three was shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents after they attempted to pull him over.

entries.title: A major housing bill is set to become law at midnight — even though Trump says he won't sign
entries.snippet: President Trump says he is refusing to sign the bill without Congress first passing his sweeping voter ID bill.

entries.title: U.S.-Iran fighting appears to pause. And, life inside Israel's military zones in Gaza
entries.snippet: Fighting between the U.S. and Iran appears to have paused after two days of clashing amid a shaky ceasefire. And, a look at what life is like inside Israel's expanding zone of control in Gaza.

entries.title: Taliban declares war on smartphones
entries.snippet: A newly announced ban on smartphones for government workers, police and military personnel is spilling over into healthcare and educational facilities. Ordinary citizens worry they'll be next.

entries.title: Waymo called the cops on teen riders, raising privacy concerns
entries.snippet: Two 15-year-olds were allegedly drinking alcohol and shooting toy guns from a driverless taxi when the company disabled it and alerted police.

entries.title: Count Binface: The intergalactic warrior who could upend Britain's strangest election
entries.snippet: Meet Count Binface: the challenger from another planet taking on Nigel Farage as questions over the Reform UK leader's finances overshadow his election comeback.

entries.title: One U.S. visa program is growing rapidly. No one is happy with it
entries.snippet: Republicans on Capitol Hill are starting to talk about one facet of immigration reform: how to expand the popular H-2A visa program for farm laborers. They face obstacles.

entries.title: 9 months into a ceasefire, Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza
entries.snippet: When the U.S. brokered a ceasefire last year, Israel controlled half of Gaza. Now Israeli forces have pushed deeper, and Palestinians are paying a deadly price.

entries.title: The EPA promised a MAHA agenda. It has yet to materialize, frustrating activists
entries.snippet: After Make America Healthy Again activists drew up a petition to get him fired, EPA administrator Lee Zeldin pledged to release a formal agenda of MAHA priorities his agency would pursue. But eight months after its first mention, the so-called MAHA agenda is nowhere to be found.

entries.title: Apple files lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing ChatGPT maker of stealing trade secrets
entries.snippet: Apple on Friday accused OpenAI of stealing trade secrets as it seeks to build its own hardware for ChatGPT, a major rupture in a partnership between the iPhone maker and the artificial intelligence company.

entries.title: Graham Platner submits notice to formally withdraw from Maine Senate race
entries.snippet: Maine is considered a key state for control of the narrowly divided Senate, and Democrats were desperate for a candidate capable of defeating Republican Sen. Susan Collins.

entries.title: A look at the new regulations and incentives in the housing bill set to become law
entries.snippet: A sweeping new housing bill is set to become law, even without the president's signature. The measure passed Congress with bipartisan support, but President Trump refused to sign it in protest of the GOP Senate's failure to approve his election legislation, known as the SAVE Act.

entries.title: What we know about Mitch McConnell's health and hospitalization
entries.snippet: There are questions surrounding the health of Sen. Mitch McConnell after the Kentucky Republican's hospitalization on June 14. Lisa Desjardins reports on what we know.

entries.title: This new bill hopes to 'put the brakes' on financial fraud targeting older Americans
entries.snippet: Financial abuse cost older victims nearly $2.4 billion in 2024, according to incidents reported to the Federal Trade Commission.

entries.snippet: The incident happened on a morning flight from the northern Greek city of Thessaloniki to Memmingen, near Munich, which was operated by Ryanair subsidiary Malta Air.

entries.title: Illnesses surge in quake-hit Venezuelan communities as humanitarian crisis builds
entries.snippet: Doctors treating people in the northern state of La Guaira on Thursday reported an increase in skin conditions and diarrheal diseases, as well as of requests for medications for the treatment of chronic illnesses, including diabetes and high blood pressure.

entries.title: Wildfire devastates southern Spain expat community, killing at least 12 with 23 missing
entries.snippet: The blaze, one of Spain's deadliest wildfires, broke out late Thursday in a semi-arid area near the Sierra de Los Filabres mountains in Almeria province, as the country has been dealing with soaring temperatures.

entries.snippet: A sizable number of English-speaking people in the U.S. are doing something these days that might be considered a bit surprising: They're watching broadcasts of World Cup matches in Spanish on Telemundo, even though they have little idea — or in some cases, no idea — what the ann

entries.title: Lawyers for man charged with killing Charlie Kirk try to sow doubt about DNA evidence
entries.snippet: A Utah judge is deciding whether prosecutors have enough evidence to put Robinson on trial on a charge of aggravated murder.

entries.title: Crews are draining the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool again as part of Trump's troubled revamp
entries.snippet: The president at first suggested his renovations would last a century. But, within weeks of the project originally reaching completion last month, the water was beset by an algae bloom and pieces of the new coating appeared to be peeling off the bottom.

entries.title: Apple sues OpenAI over stealing 'trade secrets'
entries.snippet: Apple has accused the company behind ChatGPT and two of its former employees of misappropriating its trade secrets to benefit OpenAI's foray into consumer hardware.

entries.title: Nigerian military rescues 46 abducted school children
entries.snippet: The children were abducted some two months ago at three schools in the town of Orire in Nigeria's southwestern Oyo state.

entries.title: EU threatens Meta with hefty fine over 'addictive design'
entries.snippet: A preliminary investigation by the bloc has found the social media giant is not doing enough to protect children using its platforms. Meta rejects the accusations, which could cost it 6% of its annual revenue in fines.

entries.title: Germany: Bundestag passes controversial healthcare reform
entries.snippet: The cost-cutting package has passed Germany's parliament despite fierce criticism from the opposition. Meanwhile, Alexander Zverev has become the first German man to reach the Wimbledon final since 1995. DW has more.

entries.title: Mayor of Berlin says he won't run for reelection
entries.snippet: Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner withdrew from the reelection race this fall. His decision to play tennis during the power outage in January was among missteps that has dented his reputation.

entries.title: UK police arrest murder suspect in Ann Widdecombe's death
entries.snippet: Police in southwest England say they have arrested a 26-year-old man on suspicion of murdering politician Ann Widdecombe. Based on initial inquiries, they were not treating the case as terrorism or politically motivated.

entries.title: Trump signals support for Patriot production in Ukraine
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Analysts welcome the move as a sign of support for the country — but warn it could take years before production begins.

entries.title: Ukraine's Bidnyi 'outraged' by Russia's Olympic return
entries.snippet: In exclusive comments to DW, Ukraine's sports minister, Matviy Bidnyi, said he is outraged by the IOC opening the door to Russia's return to the Olympics

entries.title: Spain: Wildfire kills several amid heat wave
entries.snippet: The victims include British and other foreign nationals, authorities have said. The Spanish royal family and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressed their deep sorrow over the loss of life.

entries.title: Passenger partly sucked from Ryanair plane during flight
entries.snippet: A man was nearly sucked out the cabin window on a Ryanair flight from Greece to Germany. An initial loud bang was followed by a desperate rescue effort to save the passenger.

entries.title: When London stank to high heaven
entries.snippet: In 1858, London sweltered through an unbearable heat wave. The River Thames reeked so badly it left people gasping for air. "The Great Stink" went down in history — and ultimately gave London a modern sewer system.

entries.title: Vietnam's baby bonuses unlikely to stop the aging clock
entries.snippet: Vietnam has joined Southeast Asia's push to raise birth rates, but experts say the greater challenge lies in adapting economies and welfare systems to an aging population.

entries.title: China retrieves booster in reusable rocket breakthrough
entries.snippet: China has joined the small group of space powers that can now recover an orbital-class booster rocket. Developers of the landing method turned to a striking alternative to that used by existing players such as SpaceX.

entries.title: Vegan pregnancy tests and other eco wins this week
entries.snippet: Keeping cool in the heat with a millennia-old tradition in India, a German company making animal-free medical tests, and building from bottles in Mozambique.

entries.title: Why the World Cup can be good for your mental health

entries.title: Germany's richest man takes on Big Tech
entries.snippet: Dieter Schwarz made his fortune from supermarkets, becoming Germany's wealthiest person. Now he wants to take on Google, Microsoft and Amazon and an entire region stands to benefit.

entries.title: Ukrainian drone strikes ignite fires at Russian oil sites
entries.snippet: An overnight assault reached key oil facilities in southern Russia, adding pressure to a fuel network already strained by repeated Ukrainian strikes.

entries.title: What's behind Germany's World Cup woes?
entries.snippet: Germany have endured three straight disappointing World Cups. Experts say the reasons why are connected to football, but also to German society.

entries.title: California’s largest lake is turning to dust
entries.snippet: The Salton Sea is drying up, worsening air pollution for people living near its shores. Authorities are working to stabilize the lakebed and lock down the dust. But for some families, it's too late.
